outcome_intro: Ask which Comet backups failed or went quiet last night and get every protected item across every tenant on your Comet Server in one list, with the error lines that explain each failure. Comet's console and emailed reports answer one customer at a time; this skill reads the whole server, reports per-tenant storage against quota, and keeps a local snapshot history so you can see what changed since yesterday.

instead_of_say.instead: Open each customer in the Comet console, or read a pile of per-job report emails, to find which backups failed, are overdue or never ran.
instead_of_say.say: Which Comet backups failed, are overdue or never ran across all my customers?

instead_of_say.instead: Open each failed job's log one at a time to find the actual error before you can decide what to fix.
instead_of_say.say: Why did last night's Comet backups fail? Group them by error.

instead_of_say.instead: Add up storage, device and Microsoft 365 counts tenant by tenant before invoicing, and find out a customer hit quota when their backup stops.
instead_of_say.say: Which tenants are at or above 80 percent of a quota?

pain_points: Comet's console and its emailed job reports work one customer and one job at a time. To answer "what failed last night across every tenant" you click through each user account or read every report email, every morning.

A backup that stops running raises no failure: a device that went offline or a schedule that never fired just goes quiet. Magnus Box, a Comet-based backup provider, tells of an MSP who lost a major client because an Exchange backup had been failing silently for two months.
The console shows today's state only, so "what changed since yesterday" and "which tenants are creeping toward quota" have no history behind them.

outcomes.question: Which protected items failed, are overdue or never backed up, across every tenant?
Why did backups fail in the last 24 hours, with the first error lines from each job log?
Which tenants are at or above 80 percent of a storage, device or Microsoft 365 quota?
Which offline devices have not finished a job in a week and still own protected items?
Which devices run a Comet client version that differs from the server?
Which backup problems opened or resolved since the previous snapshot?

different_vs_wrappers: Most Comet Backup integrations proxy one admin API call per question: fine for one user account, not for "every failed or overdue item across 60 tenants". This skill reads every user profile, device and recent job on the server in one command, works out overdue and never-ran items from each schedule, pulls the error lines from the job logs, and keeps local snapshots so what-changed questions have an answer.
different_vs_vendor: Comet has no AI assistant; its console and emailed reports show one tenant or one job at a time. This skill adds the server-wide view, the error lines and the local history on top of the same admin API, and leaves restores, policies and per-device detail where they already live in the console.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, so it needs the Comet Backup MCP server's token-protected HTTP mode hosted over HTTPS. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

faqs.q: Is my Comet Backup data safe?
faqs.a: Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server, and the local mirror are all local. The AI sees query results, not raw bulk data, and credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.q: What Comet account does it need?
faqs.a: A Comet Server admin account. Set COMET_BACKUP_SERVER to your server's host and port (or COMET_BACKUP_BASE_URL to its full URL), then COMET_BACKUP_USERNAME and COMET_BACKUP_PASSWORD. Comet recommends a dedicated API admin with a long random password and no 2FA; for an admin that requires 2FA, start a session with Comet's session-start API and set COMET_BACKUP_SESSION_KEY instead. Personal API tokens are not supported yet. On Comet-Hosted servers, create an Additional User with a local password.

faqs.q: Does it work with self-hosted and Comet-Hosted servers?
faqs.a: Yes. Each MSP runs one Comet Server, self-hosted or Comet-Hosted, holding all of its tenants; the skill talks only to the server you name and refuses a redirect to any other host.

faqs.q: Can it run backups or restores?
faqs.a: It can ask an online device to run a backup or a restore through Comet's live-connection API, but those are writes on a customer endpoint: preview them with --dry-run and keep them human-approved. The MCP server sends a write only when the call carries confirm: true. rerun-failed only prints its plan unless you add --yes.

governance_summary: Most commands only read: fleet health, failure triage, usage, device lists, job history and server status. Seven reads return credential material (password hashes, TOTP keys, storage keys); the CLI redacts those fields and the MCP server runs them only with confirm: true. Writes reach your tenants and their devices (run a backup or restore, uninstall, delete a user), so preview them with --dry-run and keep a human in the loop.
